about.intro: The REACT Task Force (Regional Endorsement Allied Computer Team) is a multi-agency task force dedicated to investigating and prosecuting high-technology crimes affecting individuals, businesses, and communities.

sections.heading: Our Mission
paragraphs: REACT works to protect the public from high-technology crime through regional collaboration, education, and law enforcement partnerships. We investigate complex cases involving cybercrime, identity theft, cryptocurrency fraud, and other technology-facilitated offenses.

sections.heading: What We Do
paragraphs: Our team of experienced investigators and analysts work across jurisdictions to combat high-tech crime. We partner with local, state, and federal agencies to pursue cases that cross traditional boundaries.
list: Investigate high-technology and computer-facilitated crimes
Provide public education and awareness about emerging threats
Collaborate with law enforcement agencies across the region
Support victims of cybercrime and identity theft

resources.intro: Find helpful resources for reporting crime, protecting yourself from fraud, and getting assistance if you've been a victim of high-tech crime.

sections.heading: Reporting Resources
paragraphs: If you believe you have been a victim of a high-tech crime, it is important to report it promptly. The following resources can help you file a report and begin the recovery process.
list: How to report a crime — step-by-step guidance for filing a report
Pig butchering awareness — learn to recognize and avoid this common scam
Victim assistance and support groups — connect with organizations that can help
Credit bureaus — protect your credit and monitor for fraudulent activity

contacts.intro: Get in touch with the REACT Task Force for inquiries, crime reporting, or general information.

sections.heading: Headquarters
paragraphs: REACT Task Force is based in San Jose, California. For general inquiries or to report a high-tech crime, please contact us using the information below.

sections.heading: Emergency
paragraphs: If you are experiencing an emergency or a crime in progress, call 911 immediately. To report a non-emergency matter, contact your local law enforcement agency.
